text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Liamine Zeroual's call for a new meeting with political parties shows his constant openness to dialogue which has earned him international and local recognition since he came to power in 1994.
- Reappointment of Ahmed Ouyahia as Prime Minister was made possible because of a constitutional clause which gives the president the power to choose the person he wants.
- Security forces have killed 10 "terrorists" during a four-day search operation near Tlemcen. Moslem rebels kill 26 civilians, including children and a pregnant woman, in two raids on villages.
- Fifteen villagers were killed in Lardjem, Tissemsilt province, including young children.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia's government expected to present his programme before parliament by mid-July.
- More than 100 girls suffer food poisoning after eating old cakes on a university campus in Algiers.
